    6. Bayesian models

    Source: vignettes/articles/bayesian.Rmd
    bayesian.Rmd

    A Bayesian model combines the data with prior knowledge and gives the whole distribution of each effect: its most likely value, a credible interval that contains it with a stated probability, and the probability that it is positive or negative. tidyvisor advises on models fitted with brms, which writes and runs the Stan code.

    library(tidyvisor)

    Before fitting 

    tidyvisor(lme4::sleepstudy, question = "bayesian", response = "Reaction",
          predictors = "Days", random = "Subject")
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'parsnip':
#>   method          from 
#>   print.nullmodel vegan
#> 
#> ── tidyvisor: which analysis? ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Question: bayesian
#> 
#> ── What the data show ──
#> 
#> • Observations: 180
#> • Response: continuous
#> • Parameters (excluding intercept): 1
#> • Levels of Subject: 18
#> 
#> ── Recommended ──
#> 
#> Model: Bayesian multilevel model with brms (gaussian())
#> A continuous, roughly symmetric response suits a linear model; check the
#> residuals after fitting. Weakly informative priors keep estimates in a
#> plausible range without dominating the data (Buerkner 2017).
#> priors <- c(brms::prior(normal(0, 2.5 * sd(y)), class = b)  # scale to the response)
#> m <- brms::brm(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), family = gaussian(), prior = priors,
#>   data = data, chains = 4, cores = 4, seed = 1)
#> Before fitting: Prior predictive check
#> Simulate from the priors alone to see that they allow plausible data and rule
#> out absurd data (Gabry et al. 2019).
#> p <- brms::brm(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), family = gaussian(), prior = priors, data = data, sample_prior = "only")
#> brms::pp_check(p)
#> After fitting: Check convergence, then the posterior predictive fit
#> R-hat must be below 1.01 and effective sample sizes above 400 before any
#> estimate is read (Vehtari et al. 2021).
#> summary(m); brms::pp_check(m); brms::loo(m)
#> Interpret: Plain-language explanation of the model
#> Effects with credible intervals and the probability of their direction.
#> tidyvisor(m)

    The advice gives the family, weakly informative priors and two checks:

    • a prior predictive check, which simulates data from the priors alone: plausible priors produce plausible data;
    • a posterior predictive check, which compares data simulated from the fitted model with the observed data.

    After fitting

    Fitting a brms model compiles a Stan program, which takes a minute or two, so the code below is shown but not run on this page.

    m <- brms::brm(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = lme4::sleepstudy,
               chains = 4, cores = 4, seed = 1)
tidyvisor(m)

    The interpretation reports, for each effect, the posterior mean, its credible interval and the probability of its direction, followed by the diagnostics that decide whether the posterior can be trusted at all:

    Diagnostic Should be If not
    R-hat below 1.01 the chains disagree: run longer or reparameterise
    Effective sample size above 400 interval limits are imprecise: more iterations
    Divergent transitions none the sampler missed part of the posterior: raise adapt_delta

    How to read the advice

    • A credible interval is a probability statement about the effect, given the model and priors; a confidence interval is not.
    • Priors matter most with few data. Report them, and check that the conclusions hold with wider priors.
    • Diagnostics first. Never read estimates from chains that have not converged.

    References

    Bürkner, P.-C. (2017). brms: an R package for Bayesian multilevel models using Stan. Journal of Statistical Software 80(1), 1-28.

    Gabry, J., Simpson, D., Vehtari, A., Betancourt, M. and Gelman, A. (2019). Visualization in Bayesian workflow. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society A 182, 389-402.

    Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B. and Bürkner, P.-C. (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: an improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC. Bayesian Analysis 16, 667-718.
